data.name: Lunch Truck Tycoon
data.detailed_description:
The Lunchinator is Here!

Welcome to Lunch Island! Where the sun always shines, everything comes in perfect individual servings and the only meal served is, LUNCH!

Head to the beach and finish the Ice Cream Sandwich event or head to the City and supply Comic Con with pretzels and coffee?

Compete in Competitions! Who has the best Hot Dog on Lunch Island? Who has the best Hot Chocolate?

Compete against other NPC’s in Cook-offs!

The Monday commute is a drag, the city must be packed. On Lunch Island, lunchers have schedules and certain locations will see more action depending on the day of the week.

It’s the weekend and lunchers like to get away to the Beach or to the Ski Resort in the mountains!

Just got a message on your cell phone that the locals in the Burbs are trying to oust the Mayor. Head there and take advantage of the influx in lunchers.

• Unlock new food items
• Unlock truck improvements
• Buy new trucks
• 55 Levels + End Game Content
• 36 Events/Quests
• 18 Competitions
• 20 Different Cook-offs
• 6 Different locations

36 food items in total and each one sells best at a specific location. Look for clues along the way that will help you recognize these locations. Knowing what items sell best at what location can be the edge you need to complete any given event or competition.

After level 55, Events, Competitions and Cook-offs will continue.

reviews.review:
I don't recommend this game.

The premise of this game is simple, a tycoon game. But as with many other tycoon games, most of them fails to deliver what is the "tycoon" itself, or what is resource management itself.

Here is why the game still need to improve :
[list]
    [*][b]No competition[/b]. There is no competition at all, it looks like you are the only one selling lunch in the island.
    [*][b]No long term business model[/b]. In tycoon games, the primary income of us should be the profit of selling goods or services. Or from re-selling other person's product or services. In this game, your primary income is awards from events, such as "Best Lemonade" or something like that.
    [*][b]Wrong micromanagement[/b]. In this game, we must adjust how much sugar, water, and lemonade in each glass of lemonade. While this seems fun, it is not. It is not fun because it is not related to the economic model. If you add some sugar, there is no increase of your "cost of goods sold", while it should be. If you reduce the amount of lemonade, your cost of goods sold should decrease, but it is not. Furthermore, this wrong micro-management only applies when you are going to enter to an event. People on the street still don't care whether you use excessive sugar or you use not enough water.
[*][b]No satisfaction model[/b]. Yes, if you increase the price people will refuses to purchase the product, but it is not clear enough. The above micro-management (managing the ingredients of the lunch item) is fun only if it is tied to the satisfaction of the customer. For example, if you use only few lemonades, the customer should refuses to buy your product. Or the customer would still buy if price is low enough. But that kind of thing does not happen in this game.
[*][b]Not enough data on nearly everything[/b]. You get a data on your profit each day. How profit is calculated? Unclear. Do you pay wages or something? Tax? No information at all. How much lemon is sold that day? How much candy is sold that day? Unclear. How to level-up and gain access to more expensive items? No information. How "high" is the traffic if I purchase a better food truck? Unclear.
 [*]It have [b]boring music and boring animation[/b]. I don't mind this, actually. But considering the above points failure, this game is not recommended.
[/list]

What is right on this game :
[list]
    [*]It is [b]cheap[/b].
    [*]It have [b]interesting concepts[/b], food truck is something fun to think about.
 [*]It is [b]easy, casual game[/b]. Note that some people (including me) will not be happy if the game is too easy.
[/list]

This game is not recommended.
